reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive deficiency of the gluconeogenic enzyme fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase (FBP1 gene) impairs glucose production from precursors such as lactate, glycerol and amino acids
Presents with episodes of hypoglycaemia accompanied by lactic acidosis and ketosis, typically triggered by fasting or intercurrent illness
First crisis often occurs in the neonatal period or first months of life, sometimes with hyperventilation, hepatomegaly and seizures
Between episodes children are usually well and grow normally, distinguishing it from the persistent features of glycogen storage disease

Unlike hereditary fructose intolerance, ingestion of fructose or sucrose can precipitate crises but there is no aversion or vomiting reflex, and the defect is in gluconeogenesis rather than fructose metabolism per se
Acute treatment uses intravenous glucose to correct hypoglycaemia and clear the lactic acidosis; long-term care emphasises avoidance of prolonged fasting and limiting fructose and sucrose intake
Diagnosis is confirmed by FBP1 molecular testing or enzyme assay, supported by the characteristic biochemical pattern during crises
reference.pathophysiology: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase catalyses a key regulatory step of gluconeogenesis, converting fructose-1,6-bisphosphate to fructose-6-phosphate. Its deficiency blocks the synthesis of glucose from lactate, glycerol, amino acids and dietary fructose, so the individual depends on dietary glucose and hepatic glycogen. Once glycogen stores are exhausted during fasting or illness, hypoglycaemia develops together with accumulation of gluconeogenic precursors, producing lactic acidosis; increased fatty-acid oxidation adds ketosis. Fructose and sorbitol loads worsen the metabolic block by trapping phosphate and further inhibiting glucose output.
additionalDifferentials: Glycogen storage disease type I (glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency)
Mitochondrial respiratory chain disorders with lactic acidosis
Fatty-acid oxidation defects presenting with hypoglycaemia
additionalInvestigations: Blood glucose, blood gas and lactate during symptomatic episodes
Blood and urine ketones to document accompanying ketosis
Urine organic acids, which may show elevated lactate and glycerol-3-phosphate
Plasma amino acids and ammonia to help distinguish other causes of metabolic acidosis
FBP1 molecular genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
Enzyme activity assay in liver or leucocytes where genetics are inconclusive
redFlags: Profound hypoglycaemia with severe lactic acidosis in a fasting or unwell infant
Hyperventilation, obtundation or seizures during a metabolic crisis
Recurrent hypoglycaemic-acidotic episodes precipitated by fasting or fructose intake
reference.prognosis: Long-term prognosis is generally good with avoidance of fasting and dietary control, and normal growth and development are usual; however, delayed recognition of severe hypoglycaemic-acidotic crises can be fatal or cause neurological injury.
pitfalls: Confusing the disorder with hereditary fructose intolerance and mismanaging dietary advice
Missing the diagnosis because the child appears entirely well between episodes
Failing to measure lactate and ketones during the acute hypoglycaemic episode
Allowing prolonged perioperative or illness-related fasting without protective glucose
references: Saudubray, Baumgartner & Walter, Inborn Metabolic Diseases: Diagnosis and Treatment
management: Treat acute crises with intravenous glucose to correct hypoglycaemia and reverse the accompanying lactic acidosis
Correct severe metabolic acidosis with intravenous bicarbonate during decompensation
Prevent crises by avoiding prolonged fasting, giving frequent carbohydrate-rich feeds and slow-release uncooked cornstarch overnight
Restrict dietary fructose, sucrose and sorbitol, which aggravate the metabolic block
Institute a sick-day emergency regimen with increased glucose intake and early hospital review during intercurrent illness
Monitor growth, blood glucose and acid-base status with dietitian-led metabolic review
Offer genetic counselling and carrier testing for this autosomal recessive disorder
